hints: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph; deceleration is the magnitude of a negative gradient.
At $t=7\,\mathrm s$ the athlete is on the straight segment whose velocity falls by $8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ over $5\,\mathrm s$.
Calculate the magnitude $|\Delta v/\Delta t|=8/5$ and state it in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the relevant segment of the velocity-time graph:
At $t = 7\text{ s}$, the athlete is on the straight line segment between $t = 5\text{ s}$ and $t = 10\text{ s}$, where the velocity changes linearly from $v = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Step 2: Calculate the acceleration as the gradient of this segment:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{0 - 8}{10 - 5} = \frac{-8}{5} = -1.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Step 3: State the deceleration:
Deceleration is the magnitude of the negative acceleration:
$$\text{Deceleration} = 1.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: Distance travelled is the total unsigned area between the velocity-time graph and the time axis.
Split the four straight-line sections at every vertex and every crossing of the time axis; areas below the axis must be added by magnitude, not subtracted.
Use triangle areas $\frac12\times\text{time base}\times\text{speed height}$; the graph can be grouped into three triangles of base $10\,\mathrm s$ and height $8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
Add those three positive areas and report the result in metres.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: State the geometric principle connecting velocity-time graphs to distance:
The total distance travelled is equal to the total area under the velocity-time graph.

Step 2: Identify the geometric components of the graph:
The graph consists of three identical triangular stages, each having base $10\text{ s}$ and height $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or six symmetrical triangles of base $5\text{ s}$ and height $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

Step 3: Calculate the total area:
$$\text{Total distance} = 3 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 8\right) = 3 \times 40 = 120\text{ m}$$
The total distance travelled by the athlete is $120\text{ m}$.
